verdict.rationale: GitLab's first-party agent docs state that you can connect a Kubernetes cluster to deploy, manage, and monitor cloud-native solutions. The same docs explicitly support communicating with clusters behind a firewall or NAT, which covers every element of the story. Missing for 10: in-depth documentation of the setup and monitoring capabilities beyond one-line statements, and independent or hands-on corroboration of firewall/NAT connectivity.

support.subject: As a devops-lead, I can connect a Kubernetes cluster, including one behind a firewall or NAT, to deploy and monitor applications

citations.quote: You can connect your Kubernetes cluster with GitLab to deploy, manage, and monitor your cloud-native solutions.
Communicate with a cluster, which is behind a firewall or NAT.
